issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:S3stitch needs alpha_R = alpha_3 never equal to -1. By the displayed formula, alpha_3 = -1 exactly when alpha_1 = 0 and sin(pi k/t + theta_1(0)) = -1, i.e. theta_1(0) lies in -pi/2 + (pi/t)Z. The stated hypothesis theta_1(0) not in {m pi - 2n pi/t} excludes a different set (the zeros of the sine at even k). Counterexample: t=1 and theta_1 constant equal to pi/2 satisfy the hypothesis, yet alpha_3(3/4) = sin(pi + pi/2) = -1. The stitched curve (eq:explicitweight3) is then undefined (division by sqrt(1+alpha_3)=0) at that parameter.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by theta_1(0) not in -pi/2 + (pi/t)Z, which is exactly what alpha_3 != -1 requires.
issues.overall_effect: The d=3 explicit statement of thm:weight is false for some parameter choices admitted by its hypothesis. Existence for d=3 is not lost, since other theta_1 work.
issues.title: Hypothesis on theta_1(0) does not guarantee alpha_3 != -1 in the explicit S^3 curve
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a hypothesis restores the statement; the construction, lengths and conclusions are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists a weighted $t$-design set on $S^d$ of size at most $D_td^{t-1}$

issues.failure_explanation: Thm weightconst needs an even-size set X on S^{d-1}, positive weights (the parameter intervals [Lambda_{i-1}, Lambda_i] must be nondegenerate), and d>1. Dillon's result only gives a weighted set of size at most D_t d^{t-1}, so the size can be odd. Making D_t even does not make |X| even. Definition def:weightset allows lambda real-valued, with no positivity. The case d=1 in the theorem statement is not covered by thm:weightconst (d>1). The proof also proves a range D > pi D_t t^d, not the stated D >= pi D_t d^{t-1}.

failure_location.quote: Then, for any $D>\pi D_tt^d$, we may pick smooth $M:[0,1]\to O(d)$ such that $w_{X,M}$ is a weighted $t$-design curve of length $D$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require positive weights, pass to an even-size set (for example use X twice with halved weights and enlarge D_t by a factor 2), treat d=1 directly, and fix the range to D >= pi D_t d^{t-1}.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof does not establish thm:weightstrength for every d and every D in the stated range.
issues.title: Weighted-set statement: parity/positivity of weights and exponent in the proof of the strength-dependence theorem
issues.why_classification: Each gap has a routine local repair that only changes the existential constant D_t.

issues.failure_explanation: The last step needs the pushforward of sigma under h(omega)=omega_1 to be (1/2)ds on [-1,1]. That holds only for S^2 (Archimedes). On S^d the density is proportional to (1-u^2)^{(d-2)/2}. Counterexample: d=3, f=omega_1^2 has degree 2 and integrates to 1/4 over S^3, but the curve gives (1/2)∫u^2 du = 1/3. The parametrization w_R is linear in s, so w_{X,M} is not a weighted t-design curve on S^d for d>=3 and t>=2. The displayed w_R also lacks the division by lambda(x_i) that the change of variables in the proof requires. The explicit d=2 and d=3 curves do not use this step beyond d=2, so they are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reparametrize each half great circle by the cumulative distribution function of the marginal density c_d(1-u^2)^{(d-2)/2}, scaled by lambda(x_i), so the time measure matches the sphere marginal. The geometric curve (semicircles, length >= pi|X|) is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The general-d existence claims (all d>1 in thm:weight, and thm:weightstrength) and the lengths pi d, 2 pi d for simplex and cross-polytope rest on a false design property. The abstract's claim for all d is unsupported.
issues.title: Construction w_{X,M} is a weighted design only for d=2: marginal of omega_1 on S^d is not uniform for d>2
issues.why_classification: The curves and length statements survive after a contained reparametrization and a corrected proof, but the stated construction and proof must be replaced for d>=3.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition pro:covrad bounds D_t, the largest nearest-neighbour distance within Y_t. That is not the covering radius rho_t of Y_t in CP^n, and it gives no upper bound on MST edge lengths. A clustered set can have tiny nearest-neighbour distances and large covering radius. The proof needs an upper bound on rho_t to get W_t <~ t^{2n-1}. Also, since epsilon_t is defined as W_t/(pi|Y_t|), the claim epsilon_t ≍ 1/t needs a lower bound W_t >~ t^{2n-1}, which is never shown. Only epsilon_t <~ 1/t follows.

failure_location.quote: noting from Proposition \ref{pro:covrad} combined with Lemma \ref{lem:poly} that $\rho_t\asymp1/t$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use (and state) a covering-radius bound rho_t <~ 1/t for design sets on CP^n, and state epsilon_t <~ 1/t (or supply a lower bound on W_t).
issues.overall_effect: The key asymptotics epsilon_t ≍ 1/t and l(gamma_t) ≍ t^{2n} in thm:main, and the even-dimensional corollary, are not justified by the cited input as stated.
issues.title: Covering radius bound is not supplied by Proposition covrad (nearest-neighbour quantity)
issues.why_classification: The theorem is plausibly salvageable by invoking the correct covering-radius estimate, but that is a different external result from the stated proposition, and the ≍ claim needs weakening or a new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We then take $W_Y$ to be double the sum of all weights of edges of $\mathcal T_Y$

issues.failure_explanation: W_Y is twice the total MST weight over |Y|-1 edges, and MST edges can be as long as about 2 rho. The correct bound is of the form W_Y <= 4(|Y|-1)rho, not rho/4. Counterexample: Y = two points at distance D = pi/2 in CP^n has W_Y = 2D = pi, but (|Y|-1)rho/4 <= pi/8. The displayed inequality is false, though only the order W_t <~ |Y_t|/t is used afterwards.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the bound by W_t <= 4(|Y_t|-1)rho_t (or any correct constant).
issues.overall_effect: The stated intermediate estimate is false; the order-of-magnitude conclusion is unaffected once the constant is corrected.
issues.title: Incorrect inequality W_t <= (|Y_t|-1) rho_t/4
issues.why_classification: Only a constant changes; the asymptotic argument is intact.

issues.failure_explanation: |sup_{S^d} f| is not a norm on P_t(S^d). It vanishes for f=-x_1^2, and it is not bounded below by |integral of f| or by (1/l) |integral over a curve of f|. The step |∫_{L\γ(l)} f - ∫_{γ|[0,1]\l} f| <= (length)·|sup f| and the equality |∫_γ f| = l(γ)|sup f| in Remark changec require sup|f|. With the literal definition, f<=0 with sup f=0 forces exact averaging, which collapses the approximate notion and makes the lemma's bound false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |sup f| by sup|f| (= ||f||_∞) in the definition and in all uses, turning the equality in Remark changec into an inequality.
issues.overall_effect: All approximate-design statements are literally stated with a degenerate error functional; the derivations of lem:overlap, rmk:changec and the later theorems are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Error term uses |sup f| (not a norm) while proofs need sup|f|
issues.why_classification: A global notational correction makes the existing proofs go through unchanged, preserving all results and rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: may be perturbed to be smooth and, if $d\neq2$, simple.

issues.failure_explanation: On S^1 a simple closed curve is a single traversal of the circle of length 2 pi. A curve gamma that winds twice (a 2t-fold cover, a t-design curve) cannot be replaced by a simple curve of length l(gamma)+delta. So the claim fails for d=1. The removal of self-intersections by 'the same procedure' is justified only by dimensional (general-position) reasoning valid for d>=3.

failure_location.quote: If $d\neq2$, we may take $\widetilde\gamma$ to be simple.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the simplicity claim to d>=3 (the case d=1 is trivial).
issues.overall_effect: The statement is false for d=1. The later uses (S^{2n+1} with n>=1) are not affected.
issues.title: Lemma smooth claims simple perturbation for all d != 2, false for d=1
issues.why_classification: A one-condition change to the statement suffices; all uses in the paper are for d>=3 or trivial.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, we see that any $(\varepsilon,c,||\cdot||_2)$-approximate $t$-design curve is a $(C_t\varepsilon,c,||\cdot||_1)$-approximate $t$-design curve.

issues.failure_explanation: The argument shows: an (eps,c,||.||_p)-approximate curve is an (eps,c,||.||_∞)-approximate curve (since ||f||_p <= ||f||_∞). Remark rmk:p claims the converse, that an eps-approximate curve (sup norm) is (eps,||.||_p)-approximate. The right side eps||f||_p is smaller than eps||f||_∞, so the L^p condition is stronger. Going from ∞ to p needs ||f||_∞ <= C_t ||f||_p with C_t growing with t (about t^{d/p}), which would destroy the rate eps_t ≍ 1/t. The Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund claims built on it are unsupported.

failure_location.quote: so we may take $C_t:=1$ to prove Remark \ref{rmk:p}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, one must prove an L^p-relative error bound for these curves directly, or accept Nikolskii-type factors and a correspondingly weaker statement with no vanishing error.
issues.overall_effect: The assertions that the curves of thm:main/thm:even are (eps_t,||.||_p)-approximate designs, and the MZ-family property for L^q (including the intro statement 'for all even q'), are not established. Remark MZ also restricts to q<=p, contradicting the intro.
issues.title: Norm comparison used in the wrong direction; L^p-approximate property and MZ claim not supported
issues.why_classification: The claim cannot be repaired by a local fix; the available norm-equivalence constants depend on t and worsen the error rate, so the advertised L^p/MZ guarantee is lost.
